channel.title: Boulder Daily Camera - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Boulder Daily Camera (dailycamera.com)

item.title: Boulder files complaint against former City Council candidate over alleged unspent funds
item.description: City says Aaron Stone owes about $375 in unspent funds, an amount that Stone disputes.

item.title: Overhauled roster, staff as Deion Sanders, CU Buffs open spring practice
item.description: Deion Sanders is entering his fourth season at Colorado ready to do something he’s done plenty of times before: rebuild.

item.title: No. 15 Colorado lacrosse uses fast start to defeat No. 22 Army
item.description: In a two-game road trip against ranked foes, the Colorado women’s soccer team salvaged a split.

item.title: Colorado women’s basketball nabs No. 6 seed for Big 12 Tournament
item.description: The Colorado women’s basketball team left Provo, Utah, on Saturday afternoon knowing it fumbled an opportunity. Twice.

item.title: Colorado Buffaloes quarterback Dominiq Ponder dies at age 23
item.description: University of Colorado football player Dominiq Ponder died early Sunday morning in a single vehicle crash. He was 23 years old.

item.title: 3 US troops killed and 5 are seriously wounded during Iran attacks, military says
item.description: U.S. Central Command announced the deaths but didn't say when and where they occurred.

item.title: Stranded travelers scramble to make new connections as war shuts much of Middle East to air travel
item.description: FlightAware reported more than 2,800 flights were canceled Sunday across major Middle Eastern airports.

item.title: Oil prices rise sharply in market trading after attacks in Middle East disrupt global energy supply
item.description: Traders were betting the supply of oil could slow or grind to a halt.

item.title: At least 22 people killed in Pakistan as protesters try to storm US Consulate
item.description: The violence came after the attack on Iran.

item.title: Front Range sends six hoops teams to the 6A and 5A quarterfinals
item.description: Colorado girls basketball’s all-time scoring leader. The state’s winningest coach. This winter’s leading scorer. Local girls will face all of them in the Sweet 16.
